tasks.title: Implement metadata keyset pagination
tasks.objective: Return validated authenticated cursor pages using explicit metadata SQL projection without parsing project payloads.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Estimate covers repository projection, query and cursor validation, route adaptation and focused tests. The inspected code is small, but boundary behavior is new and depends on D1. No comparable history is available.

complexity.justification: Keyset pagination combines tuple comparisons, lookahead and hostile query validation.

scope.justification: Pagination is confined to the list repository method, HTTP route and focused tests.

duration.justification: Repository fixtures exist but pagination and HTTP boundary cases require new coverage.
evidence: assumption:One hundred minutes is an uncalibrated focused implementation estimate.

risk.justification: Changing the existing list endpoint alters an externally consumed API contract.

coupling.justification: The project-list-contract produced by T2 is implemented here and consumed by T4.

confidence.justification: SQL, HTTP errors and authentication were inspected but pagination semantics await D1.

acceptance_criteria: After D1 resolution, accept optional single-string limit and cursor parameters; proposed limits are default 50 and maximum 100.
Authenticate before validation; malformed limits, repeated or structured parameters and invalid cursor encoding, size, version or shape return HTTP 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.
Use explicit metadata columns, bound parameters and updated_at DESC then id DESC ordering; continuation seeks updated_at below the anchor or equal updated_at with id below the anchor.
Fetch limit plus one rows, emit at most limit items and encode the last emitted tuple only when a further row exists; empty and terminal pages return nextCursor null.
Do not select data_json or invoke snapshot parsing for list results; a deleted cursor anchor does not prevent continuation.
Preserve detail snapshots, mutation revisions and existing authentication behavior without a database migration.

verification.value: npm run build -w @training/contracts && npm run test -w @training/api
verification.purpose: Verify new pagination cases for empty, exact-size, lookahead, tied timestamp, deleted anchor and invalid query boundaries.

verification.value: Review the list SQL, cursor decoder and route error paths.
verification.purpose: Verify projection and algorithm properties not established by response typing alone.
verification.expected: Only metadata columns are read; SQL is parameterized; tuple comparison matches ordering; authentication precedes validation; snapshot methods remain separate.

tasks.title: Preserve complete web project discovery
tasks.objective: Adapt the browser list helper to consume all cursor pages atomically so project screens and tab reconciliation retain complete-list semantics.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Estimate includes shared-schema parsing, traversal guards, component refresh sequencing and tests using the existing API TypeScript runner. Screen validation is separate in T5; no comparable history is available.

complexity.justification: Complete-list adaptation must coordinate asynchronous traversal, failures and tab reconciliation.

scope.justification: The helper and its two known screen consumers form a bounded browser change.

duration.justification: Existing fetch logic is compact but traversal failures need additional focused tests.
evidence: assumption:Ninety minutes is provisional and excludes browser product verification.

risk.justification: Partial enumeration could hide projects and incorrectly remove persisted browser tabs.

coupling.justification: The web-complete-project-list adapter consumes T3 pages and supplies T5 integration checks.

confidence.justification: Both list consumers were inspected but the new traversal requires unexecuted verification.

acceptance_criteria: Keep listProjects returning an object with projects to existing consumers while fetching pages sequentially until explicit nextCursor null.
Establish the session once per traversal, validate page schemas and encode cursor query values.
Accumulate privately and reject malformed pages, page failures and repeated cursors without resolving a partial list.
Deduplicate project IDs using higher revision values while preserving first encounter position; do not promise a snapshot under concurrent updates.
Only the latest refresh updates each component; failed traversal retains prior project and tab state and does not infer deletion from partial results.
Add controlled-fetch tests loading the actual web helper through the existing API tsx test runner without introducing dependencies.

verification.purpose: Exercise the real web helper across multiple pages, terminal null, duplicate IDs, repeated cursors, malformed pages and later-page failures.
Verify both existing consumers remain compatible with the complete-list helper and shared item type.

interfaces.title: Project list cursor page
inputs: Authenticated GET /v1/projects with D1-validated optional limit and cursor.
outputs: A strict page containing projects with exactly id, externalKey, name, revision and updatedAt, plus nextCursor string or null.
invariants: D1 must be resolved before implementation; proposed defaults are 50 items and maximum 100.
Ordering and seeking use updated_at DESC then id DESC with parameterized tuple predicates and limit-plus-one lookahead.
No project data_json is selected or parsed for listing; detail endpoints retain snapshots.
Invalid pagination returns 400 VALIDATION_ERROR after authentication.
Stable datasets traverse completely without duplicates; concurrent mutation does not imply snapshot consistency.
External compatibility and notice fulfillment cannot be established by local schema or HTTP tests.
integration_criteria: HTTP tests verify exact metadata shapes, tied timestamp traversal, terminal null and invalid inputs.
The web adapter validates and consumes this page format without exposing a partial enumeration.
Migration guidance matches the verified wire contract.

interfaces.title: Complete web project enumeration
inputs: Successive validated IF-1 pages obtained after establishing a browser session.
outputs: A resolved listProjects result containing the complete aggregated projects array, or a rejected traversal.
invariants: No partial result is published before explicit terminal null.
Repeated cursors, malformed pages and page errors reject the traversal.
Duplicate IDs retain higher revision values in first encounter position.
Only the latest refresh updates component state; a failed traversal preserves prior list and tabs.
Absence from a partial page is never interpreted as project deletion.
integration_criteria: Controlled-fetch tests exercise multiple pages and failure guards using the actual helper.
Screen verification demonstrates later-page discovery, persisted tab retention, name refresh and actual deletion reconciliation.
